cells.tense: You are steady without hardening, and what you're holding stays held because you keep holding it.
cells.ask: Take one thing you handle alone and put a day or a limit on it — written down, where you'll see it.
cells.core:
You're holding something and it isn't cracking. What's happening is pressure — material, real, the kind that shows up in the body and in the middle of the month — and it's meeting something in you that keeps going anyway.

You know the difference between steady and stiff. Staying steady next to people quietly is the real article; steady that has to win has already slipped. You're close to that line, and noticing it is the work. The record doesn't know what you're carrying or how long. That's yours, and so is what you do with it next.
cells.sheetLine: You're steady, and the steadiness isn't making you hard.

cells.tense: You are bracing for a pressure that hasn't arrived yet, and the bracing is doing its own damage.
cells.ask: Name one load you've taken on 'because someone has to' — then hand it back to the person who has to.
cells.core:
You can see the trouble coming from far off, so you've already picked up the weight of it. Not the load that's here now — the one next month, the one that might land on a person you're responsible for.

That's the same steady grip, aimed forward. It reads as strength and costs like fear. In private it looks like staying ahead, and it ends up spending your endurance on things nobody has handed you. The hold itself is fine. What it needs is a limit: one thing at a time, one round at a time. Then giving and getting start to even out, and you can put something down without feeling like you've failed a charge.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying weight that hasn't been handed to you yet.

cells.tense: Something ended and you're still standing at the doorway, holding the stance that got you through it.
cells.ask: Tell one person about a thing you did that nobody saw — not to process it, just as a fact, out loud.
cells.core:
You got through something, and the habit of doing it alone stuck. You can keep going, and the going has gone flat. The stance is still up and there's nothing in front of it.

What's absent here isn't more endurance. It's somebody saying yes, that happened, and you did that. Whether that comes from one person or from your own records doesn't matter. Once it's out in the open, the stance can loosen, and the room around you can become what you build in rather than what you stand against. The record doesn't know what you're standing in or how long it's been there. That part stays yours.
cells.sheetLine: You did something nobody saw. You can stop carrying it alone now.

cells.tense: You are already building the arrangement that keeps things workable, and you talk about it as if it happened by itself.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once, what you decided — then let yourself notice that you were the one deciding.
cells.core:
Look at what actually works around you. The rhythm, the order you keep, the fact that things get done on the day they're due — none of that is luck. Somebody arranged it. You arranged it.

But it doesn't get said, not even to you. So it feels like just how things are, and it isn't. The arrangement is fine. What's missing is the mention. The point isn't credit — it's that the same hand that can keep a system running can also hope past it, and that only happens if you're holding the pen. The record can't tell you why it went unnamed. Naming it is one sentence.
cells.sheetLine: You're running the thing. You just haven't claimed it yet.
